verdict.reasoning: Headache for ~3 days and worse around right eye: patient says, “Around three days ago, maybe” and “mainly around my right eye.” Severity implied as significant: “really crazy headache … pretty… a lot” and rated 8/10 later.
Duration and pattern: “Around three days ago, maybe” and “it kind of comes and goes, but I mean, it is there all the time, but like sometimes it's stronger.” Severity: “It's probably an 8.”
Patient description: “It's kind of. It's dull, but sometimes it gets a bit sharper.”

Onset and progression: “it like it developed gradually, I guess. It's like the first day it just started when I was at work and by the end of the day it was… a lot… Then I woke up the next morning like it was even, even worse.”
Photophobia: patient says bright lights hurt — “now like light is quite annoying my eyes.” Doctor clarifies, “does it hurt to look at bright lights?” Patient: “Yeah, yeah, it hurts.”
Visual phenomenon: “just when it started I got this like weird shooting lights.”
No vision loss: Doctor asks, “have you had any loss of vision or blurry vision?” Patient: “Not loss of vision, I wouldn't say. It's just like some lights from shooting light speed.”

Nausea without vomiting: Doctor asks, “Any nausea or any vomiting?” Patient: “basically I'm sick with the headache, but I. No vomiting.” Doctor clarifies “you feel sick? Okay? Yeah, No vomiting.” Feeling sick here indicates nausea.
Neck stiffness denied: Doctor asks, “Any neck pain or neck stiffness?” Patient: “No.”
No speech/motor deficits: Doctor asks, “any difficulty with speaking or speech?” and “Any difficulty with weakness in your arms and legs?” Patient answers “No” to both.
No fever: Doctor asks, “Any temperatures or fevers?” Patient: “No.”
No rash: Doctor asks, “Any rashes at all on your skin?” Patient: “No, none of that I've noticed.”
No head trauma: Doctor asks, “Any recent head injuries at all?” Patient: “No.”
Ibuprofen use: Patient says, “I tried ibuprofen… I took like a few for the last two days… But it doesn't really help.” Later, dosing clarified: “How many tablets…?” “Three a day.”
No significant PMH: Doctor asks, “Do you have any other medical history?” Patient: “I think so. It's just a headache.” No surgical history is mentioned, so absence is consistent.
No prior migraines: Doctor asks, “Any history of migraines at all?” Patient: “Not myself. I've never had a migraine, but my sister and my mum have them quite frequently.”
No regular meds: Doctor asks, “do you take any regular medication?” Patient: “No.”
No known drug allergies: Doctor asks, “Do you have any allergies to any medications?” Patient: “Not that I know of.”
Mother with migraines: Patient: “my sister and my mum have them quite frequently.” Later elaborated about mother’s migraines with seasons.
Sister with migraines: same statement: “my sister and my mum have them quite frequently.”

Work and stress: Patient: “I work in it, so I work with computers a lot… it kind of is difficult to focus.” Stress: Doctor asks about stress; patient: “it's been a bit stressful kicking off a new project, but yeah, nothing out of the ordinary really.”
Glasses and eye exam: Doctor asks, “Do you wear glasses?” Patient: “Yes, I do.” “Have you had a recent eye check…?” Patient: “No, I've been wearing them since I was five.”
Living situation: Doctor: “Who lives at home with you?” Patient: “I live with housemates, so three of them.”
Social smoking: Doctor asks, “regarding smoking… do you drink or smoke at all?” Patient: “I socially smoke and I drink.”

Transcript: Patient clarifies, “I socially smoke and I drink. Not only socially.” Doctor repeats, “Only socially.” The patient explicitly says drinking is not only social, so saying “drinks alcohol socially” alone is inaccurate.

Doctor’s assessment: “I do think this could be a headache very similar to migraine… given your mum and your sister also have migraines.” Features include photophobia and family history, and lack of response to ibuprofen: “But it doesn't really help.” This matches a probable migraine-type headache with those features.
Tension headache is never mentioned as a differential in the transcript.
Cluster headache is never mentioned or discussed in the transcript.
Doctor says only, “You can take up to two tablets three times a day.” No specific strength (400 mg) or 6–8 hour interval is discussed.
Doctor: “I can give you a prescription for that today” referring to codeine after patient mentions, “I think codeine is what my mom takes.”
Doctor: “I can prescribe you something stronger like naproxen… which can be helpful.” This indicates naproxen was discussed as an option.
Doctor: “We can also add in other painkillers like paracetamol or codeine, which might be helpful as well.”
Reducing screen brightness was mentioned as something the patient already did, not as an explicit doctor recommendation; hydration or resting in a dark room are never discussed as advice.
Doctor: “it may be worth keeping a headache diary so we can try and work out what's… If there's any triggers.”
Doctor: “If you are having more frequent episodes… we can think about giving you medications as prophylactic… to stop you from having these headaches on a regular basis.”
Eye test advice: “if you feel like your eyes are straining, I would always recommend having a repeat eye test done.”
Follow-up: “I'd like you to come back and see me in about a week's time. Week to two weeks time.”

Safety-net: “if your headaches aren't getting any better or they're getting worse… give me a call or come back and see me sooner… If you have any problems with your vision or weakness in your arms and legs, or you're just not feeling very well, just give me a call and come back and see me.”
